headline: Elevated risk today; AEMO sees spikes our model does not
summary: Our central forecast averages $95/MWh today, peaking at $153/MWh at 17:45, with a risk ceiling of $280/MWh at the same time, below the $300/MWh spike threshold. AEMO's outlook is much higher, averaging $153/MWh ($58/MWh above our central) with a $616/MWh peak in the half-hour ending 18:00 and 5 half-hours at or above $300/MWh. In backtests AEMO is closer on typical half-hours but sometimes projects high prices that do not happen.
key_points: Risk level is elevated. Today's low is $16/MWh at 10:40 and demand peaks at 7882 MW at 18:35.
Yesterday averaged $203/MWh with one spike interval reaching $23200/MWh.
Tomorrow looks softer: central average $76/MWh, max $106/MWh at 17:25, risk ceiling $166/MWh, despite demand peaking at 10410 MW at 16:50.
Track record over 6 days: normal MAE $29/MWh vs $48/MWh naive; the risk ceiling covered 84% of outcomes. Market regime is similar to the training period.

headline: High risk today: AEMO projects extreme prices, our central far lower
summary: Risk level is high today: our central forecast averages $110/MWh, peaking at $157/MWh at 20:20, but the risk ceiling reaches $426/MWh at 17:00 and sits at or above the $300/MWh spike threshold for 4.2 hours. AEMO's outlook is dramatically higher, averaging $5388/MWh with a $23200/MWh peak for the half-hour ending 18:00. In backtests AEMO is closer on typical half-hours but sometimes projects high prices that do not happen. Tomorrow looks calmer, with a central average of $69/MWh and a risk ceiling that peaks at $183/MWh.
key_points: Today: central ranges from $29/MWh at 09:05 to $157/MWh at 20:20. Demand peaks at 9884 MW at 17:55, close to the risk ceiling high of $426/MWh at 17:00.
AEMO outlook: 12 half-hours at or above $300/MWh, with an average $5278/MWh above our central. This is a large gap, so treat the evening window with caution.
Tomorrow: central ranges from -$1/MWh at 13:15 to $116/MWh at 20:20. No hours have a risk ceiling at spike level, and demand peaks at 8399 MW at 18:55.

Track record (6 days): normal-period MAE is $36/MWh versus $73/MWh for the naive forecast. The risk ceiling covered actual prices 79% of the time, and the market regime is similar to the training period.
